result.question:
Produce a decision-useful DESIGN & ENGINEERING brief for a touch-first, iPhone-first "Arrange" timeline in Echoel (a bio-reactive music+visual instrument, Swift/AVFoundation/Metal, zero heavy deps) that lets users cut/edit MIDI, AUDIO and VIDEO on ONE musical beat grid — with snap-to-beat AND stepless (free) positioning — easy for beginners yet professional, future-proof and long-term usable for ALL skill levels. Research the ACTUAL interaction models of the reference apps and extract concrete, adoptable patterns. Cover exactly:

1) WAVEFORM RENDERING (proper WAV display): how pro DAWs/NLEs render audio waveforms — peak/RMS overview caching, min/max per pixel-column, multi-resolution/mipmap zoom, stereo vs mono, linear vs log amplitude, color/opacity conventions, and drawing performance on mobile GPUs (Metal). What makes a waveform read as "professional" vs "toy". Reference: Ableton Live, Logic/GarageBand, Reaper, FL Studio, Cubase/Cubasis, Serato/rekordbox, iZotope RX.

2) CLIP EDITING & SNAP MODEL: snap-to-grid vs free/stepless move; how apps let you TEMPORARILY bypass snap (desktop hold-modifier; the TOUCH equivalent), adjustable snap resolution (bar/beat/1-16/triplet/ticks), nudge, magnetic edges, ripple/roll/slip/slide edits, crossfades/fades on clip edges, quantize-clip-to-bar, warp/time-stretch to tempo. What the DEFAULT should be so a beginner isn't confused but a pro isn't limited.

3) VIDEO ON A MUSICAL TIMELINE: how video NLEs and music-video tools cut video in time with music — track-based vs Final Cut's magnetic timeline, J/L cuts, thumbnail/filmstrip rendering, beat-marker overlays, snapping clips to detected beats. Reference: DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, Final Cut Pro (incl. iPad), CapCut, LumaFusion (iPhone/iPad), Resolume Arena. How to keep video-cut-to-beat approachable.

4) TOUCH-FIRST TIMELINE UX (critical — iPhone-first): how the best MOBILE editors handle finger editing on a small timeline — pinch-to-zoom, two-finger scroll, drag handles/trim, the magnet/snap toggle, long-press context, precision without a mouse, avoiding fat-finger errors, haptics. Reference: GarageBand iOS, Cubasis, BeatMaker 3, Auria Pro, Koala, LumaFusion, CapCut mobile, Final Cut for iPad.

5) ALL SKILL LEVELS / PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: how tools serve beginners AND pros without being two apps — smart defaults, optional grids, simple-vs-advanced modes, GarageBand→Logic continuity, onboarding. What long-term-proof, future-oriented (incl. spatial/XR timeline hints) choices to make now.

Deliverable: (a) a prioritized list of concrete interaction patterns Echoel should ADOPT for its touch Arrange timeline (the snap+free-move model, gestures, defaults); (b) a technical approach for waveform rendering on iOS/Metal that is shippable in Swift; (c) a video-cut-to-beat approach that stays approachable; and (d) an explicit "keep it simple" guardrail list — what NOT to copy from pro tools that would overwhelm beginners. Cite sources and effect/ならび where they exist. Ground everything in what is actually shippable on an iPhone with Swift/AVFoundation/Metal.
result.summary: For Echoel's touch-first Arrange timeline, the strongest, best-sourced pattern to adopt is GarageBand iOS's zoom-coupled snap model: snap-to-grid is the default at normal zoom, and free/stepless positioning is unlocked by pinch-zooming to maximum and pinching again (a visible "Snap to Grid off" state), re-enabled by zooming out — a touch-native substitute for the desktop hold-modifier that works identically for MIDI notes and audio/video region clips. For video-cut-to-beat, Final Cut Pro's opt-in per-clip Beat Detection (which analyzes a music clip, draws a bar/beat grid, and binds edit points to it only when snapping is on) is the approachable model, and it already ships a touch equivalent on FCP for iPad (touch-and-hold clip → Enable Beat Detection). For shippable waveform rendering on iOS/Metal, the confirmed approach is offline downsampling into bucketed summary data — min/max-per-pixel-column plus a stacked peak+average (RMS) envelope, precomputed per zoom tier (MaxChannel/AvgChannel) because raw PCM (~100 MB per 10 min stereo 44.1 kHz) is impractical to draw directly — fed by Accelerate/vDSP (e.g. vDSP_desamp) into Metal. Note that the surveyed live-visualizer Accelerate/Metal tutorial transfers to Echoel's real-time pipeline but NOT to scrollable overview caching.

findings.claim: Adopt GarageBand iOS's zoom-coupled snap model: snap-to-grid is the DEFAULT at normal zoom, and stepless/free positioning is unlocked by pinch-zooming to maximum then pinching again (a persistent 'Snap to Grid off' state shown atop the Tracks area), and restored by pinch-zooming out. This is the touch-native equivalent of a desktop hold-modifier, and it applies equally to audio/video region clips AND individual MIDI notes.
findings.vote: unanimous (4 claims, all 3-0 except none dissenting)
findings.evidence: Primary Apple Support doc 101913 states verbatim: 'To turn off Snap to Grid, pinch-zoom to the maximum level... Pinch-zoom again and "Snap to Grid off" will appear on top of the Tracks area' and 'To turn Snap to Grid back on, pinch-zoom out.' Apple also confirms it works for both regions and notes ('If you are editing notes in a region, you can also turn off Snap to Grid'). Caveat surfaced by verifiers: it is a latched MODE toggled at max zoom, not a momentary hold-during-drag modifier — the analogy is functional, not literal. Design implication for Echoel: keep snap on by default; couple free-placement to a high-magnification view where fine placement is actually visible; consider offering BOTH the zoom-coupled gesture and an explicit magnet toggle so pros aren't forced to max-zoom.

findings.claim: Adopt Final Cut Pro's Beat Detection as the video-cut-to-beat model: an OPT-IN, per-clip analysis (menu / Option-B / inspector checkbox on desktop; touch-and-hold clip → Enable Beat Detection on iPad) that auto-analyzes a music clip and draws a beat grid of song parts, bars, and beats — NOT hand-placed markers. Edit points bind to that grid only when snapping is turned on, so snapping is the mechanism that ties cuts to detected beats.
findings.vote: 3-0 (except the 'snapping is required' mechanism claim which was 2-1)
findings.evidence: Apple FCP guide: 'Beat Detection intelligently analyzes music clips and displays a beat grid, letting you quickly and easily align edits with song parts, bars, and beats,' enabled via 'Clip > Enable Beat Detection (or press Option-B),' and 'To easily align items with the beat grid, turn on snapping.' The iPad guide gives the touch gesture: 'Touch and hold a selected music clip, then tap Enable Beat Detection.' Being per-clip opt-in (with an inspector checkbox) keeps it approachable — beginners never see a beat grid until they ask for one. Minor verifier nuance: 'requires snapping' slightly overstates (one could eyeball), but Apple presents snapping as THE binding mechanism. For Echoel: analyze the bio-driven/musical track, overlay a beat grid, and let video clips snap to those beats when the magnet is on.

findings.claim: For shippable iOS waveform rendering, precompute bucketed summary data offline — never draw raw PCM. Split the signal into regular time intervals and, per pixel-column, keep the min and max (preserving visual extremes) plus an average/RMS value, drawing a stacked two-layer envelope (peak outline + inner RMS body) per track. Precompute multiple zoom-tier summaries and select which is drawn by zoom level (e.g. MaxChannel/AvgChannel style abstraction).
findings.vote: mixed: min/max-per-column 3-0, 100MB/impracticality 3-0, zoom-tier architecture 3-0; the 'avg+max stacked' bucketing 2-1
findings.evidence: Primary technique corroborated beyond the single iOS blog: Audacity Manual (dark layer = tallest peak, light layer = RMS average, drawn one over the other), NAudio WaveFormRendering, BBC audiowaveform, and iZotope RX all use min/max-per-block downsampling with multi-resolution peak caches. Arithmetic confirms raw PCM is impractical: 44,100 Hz x 2 ch x 2 bytes x 600 s ≈ 100 MB. The zoom-tiered abstraction (abstract Channel with Max/Avg subclasses swapped per zoom) is a working, shippable pattern (denivip repo). Verifier correction to note: pro tools store min AND max (symmetric envelope) and use RMS (raw AC 'average' ≈ 0), not plain average — Echoel should compute RMS for the inner body, min/max for the outline. 'Professional' waveform reads come from preserved extremes + RMS body + crisp per-pixel-column resolution at every zoom; downsampling that loses peaks reads as 'toy.'

findings.claim: Use Accelerate/vDSP as the signal-reduction stage feeding a Metal-rendered timeline. vDSP_desamp can collapse many audio samples into few pixel columns (with an equal-coefficient FIR filter it yields a per-column average); vDSP is Apple's own highly-optimized DSP-over-large-arrays framework. Pipeline: AVAudioEngine → Accelerate/vDSP → Metal.
findings.evidence: Blog + Apple primary docs (accelerate, WWDC 2019 session 718) confirm vDSP is hand-tuned DSP over large vectors and that vDSP_desamp performs FIR filtering with decimation; an all-equal-coefficient filter makes each output the average of contributing inputs (independently confirmed by Limit Point 'PlotAudio'). IMPORTANT scoping caveat from verifiers: the surveyed tutorial is a REAL-TIME loudness/FFT visualizer, NOT an offline scrollable waveform-overview renderer — its patterns transfer to Echoel's live bio-reactive visual pipeline but NOT directly to peak/RMS overview caching for the Arrange timeline. For the timeline, pair vDSP reduction with the offline min/max-per-column + RMS caching above, and note pro practice favors min/max-per-column over pure averaging for the visible outline.

result.caveats: Source strength is uneven. The two strongest findings (GarageBand snap model, FCP Beat Detection) rest on PRIMARY Apple documentation and are unanimous — high confidence and directly shippable-as-pattern. The waveform-rendering and vDSP findings lean on iOS engineering BLOGS (denivip 2016, a Better Programming Medium tutorial) for their framing, though the CORE techniques (min/max-per-column, 100MB PCM impracticality, RMS+peak stacked layers) are independently corroborated by Audacity, NAudio, BBC audiowaveform, and iZotope — so the techniques are solid even where the specific sources are blog-quality; confidence is capped at medium because of source authority, not technical doubt. Two verifier corrections must carry into implementation: (1) pro waveforms store min AND max plus RMS, not plain 'average' (raw AC average ≈ 0) — one refuted claim already tried to over-generalize RMS as the single best per-column measure; (2) the surveyed vDSP/Metal tutorial is a live FFT visualizer, so it does NOT directly solve scrollable overview caching. GarageBand's snap-off is a latched mode toggled at max zoom, not a literal momentary hold-modifier — the desktop analogy is functional, not exact. Time-sensitivity: Apple UI/gesture behaviors (GarageBand iOS, FCP iPad) are current as of July 2026 and long-stable, but menu paths/shortcuts can shift across app versions. The research did NOT independently verify Ableton, Reaper, FL Studio, Cubasis, LumaFusion, CapCut, or Resolume interaction specifics with surviving citations — those references in the brief remain uncorroborated by this verification pass.
openQuestions: What is the concrete TOUCH gesture for TEMPORARILY (momentary) bypassing snap during an active drag on mobile — as opposed to GarageBand's latched max-zoom mode toggle? No surviving claim documents a true hold-to-suspend-snap gesture for touch, which is the exact interaction Echoel most needs to pin down.

How should adjustable snap RESOLUTION (bar / beat / 1-16 / triplet / ticks) be exposed on a phone-sized timeline without a menu-heavy UI — and what should the beginner-safe DEFAULT resolution be? Not covered by any verified claim.

What are the actual verified interaction models of the other cited touch editors (Cubasis, BeatMaker 3, LumaFusion, CapCut mobile) for trim handles, ripple/slip/slide edits, crossfades, and haptics? None survived verification, so the 'keep it simple / what NOT to copy' guardrail list lacks sourced grounding.

For the Metal implementation specifically: what is the recommended peak-cache file format, on-device generation cost, and incremental/streaming update strategy for long clips on an iPhone — the verified sources establish the technique but not mobile performance budgets or a caching schema.

refuted.claim: For audio loudness/amplitude reduction, the tutorial recommends Accelerate's vDSP root-mean-square (RMS) calculation as the best-fit measurement, because RMS averages a function that swings above and below zero and is a well-established loudness technique — directly adoptable for reducing raw samples to per-column waveform values.
